SPF persistent-hop protocol v1 (all integers little-endian)

Capabilities (all must equal literal "1"):
  iio,buffer-persistent-hop
  iio,buffer-persistent-hop-request
  iio,buffer-persistent-hop-event
  iio,buffer-persistent-hop-status
  iio,buffer-persistent-hop-cancel

In-band cancel command:
  CANCELBUFM <device>\r\n
  The server synchronously invokes cancel_restore and returns its normal signed
  integer reply (0 on an attested successful restore). It retains the open
  buffer and transport so READBUFMSTAT can return HOPT before CLOSE.

HOPR request suffix: 288 bytes
  0 u32 magic HOPR; 4 u16 version; 6 u16 bytes
  8 u32 features=0x1f; 12 u32 flags=0x03
  16 session_id; 24 sample_rate_hz; 32 rf_bandwidth_hz
  40 i64 if_offset_hz; 48 dwell_samples; 56 transition_guard_samples
  64 dwell_count hard bound; 72 u16 profile_count=8
  74 u8 initial_profile=0; 75 reserved=0
  76 u16 event_bytes=80; 78 u16 status_bytes=160
  80..87 reserved=0; 88 u64 capture_span_samples
  96 + i*24: u8 id=i, u8 fastlock slot, u16 reserved,
                u64 center_hz, u64 lo_hz, u32 profile_crc32
  Profile order: CH1L CH2L CH3L CH4L CH1U CH2U CH3U CH4U.

HOPS sidecar: 64-byte header plus 0..8 80-byte event records
  header: magic/version/header=64/record bytes/features/flags,
          event count/capacity=8/session/buffer sequence/block first/block end,
          state/reason/error
  event: sequence/dwell index/transition before/transition after/
         invalid start/invalid end/from/to/kind/flags/slot/reserved/
         actual LO/i64 actual IF/device event id

HOPT status: fixed 160 bytes. See spf-hop-protocol.h for the field map.

Every counter and tuning attestation in an event or receipt is device evidence.
iiOD must never substitute host time or an inferred buffer boundary.
For each retune, invalid_start is the scheduled end of the prior valid dwell;
the transition is conservatively bounded by:
  invalid_start <= transition_before <= transition_after <= invalid_end
and invalid_end == transition_after + transition_guard_samples. Scheduler
lateness is therefore invalid rather than being misclassified as useful data.
Each nonterminal visit proves exactly dwell_samples useful samples:
  next.invalid_start - current.invalid_end == dwell_samples
Planned completion proves the last visit the same way:
  final_counter - last.invalid_end == dwell_samples
